question.text: Under SEBI ICDR Regulations, which of the following categories is explicitly INELIGIBLE to be identified as a Social Enterprise for SSE registration?

answer.text: A rural healthcare NPO providing maternal services in aspirational districts
A corporate foundation set up by a listed conglomerate, a political organisation, and an infrastructure / housing company (except affordable housing)
A Section 8 company engaged in slum area development in Mumbai
An FPE enhancing small-and-marginal-farmer income in non-farm sectors

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pp.17 and 76, corporate foundations, political or religious organisations and activities, professional or trade associations, and infrastructure and housing companies (except affordable housing) are explicitly ineligible to be identified as Social Enterprises for SSE registration. The Trap: Options A, C and D each map to one of the eligible activity categories (healthcare, slum development, rural livelihood). Only Option B lists the explicitly ineligible classes. A common error is treating corporate foundations as eligible — the workbook is clear they are not. Note: The ineligibility list applies even if the entity's activities appear to align with the eligible activity categories.
